correctness.rationale: The finite Riesz-lattice expression for each element of the generated sublattice is a difference of two finite maxima of algebraic tensors; each point therefore lies in one of finitely many closed coincidence sets with a fixed algebraic branch. Baire gives an open interior rectangle where an analytic kernel agrees with a finite-rank branch. Choose a basis of local sections, linearly independent evaluations and invert the evaluation matrix to obtain globally continuous, interior-analytic coefficient functions. The analytic residual vanishes on an open rectangle in the connected interior, hence identically by real-analytic identity theorem; continuity propagates to boundary. Handles rank zero and requires full connected analyticity, not merely smoothness.
